company_understanding.how_company_makes_money: Apple sells hardware (iPhone, Mac, iPad and other products) and monetizes an installed base of over 2.5 billion active devices through Services. In the latest reported quarter (FY2026 Q3, ended 2026-06-27), total revenue was $109.417B, with Products revenue of $78.7B (up 18% YoY, driven by double-digit growth in iPhone and Mac) and Services revenue of $30.7B (up 12% YoY, with records in every services category). Company gross margin was 50.1% and operating margin 32.62%. TTM revenue is $466.823B with 14.24% YoY growth and TTM EPS of $8.71 (up 29.94% YoY).
company_understanding.largest_growth_driver: Services growth and continued iPhone/Mac product momentum. Management highlighted Services revenue of $30.7B, up 12% YoY, with all-time records in cloud services and payment services, and Products revenue up 18% YoY driven by double-digit iPhone and Mac growth. The installed base reached another all-time high across all major product categories and geographies.
company_understanding.largest_operating_risk: Tariff-related costs and supply constraints pressuring gross margin and revenue timing. Management cited approximately $800 million in tariff-related costs in the June quarter, with Products gross margin down 140 bps sequentially, and noted supply constraints on iPhone and, to a lesser extent, Mac in the March quarter.

pm_synthesis.current_view: AAPL shows strong reported operating momentum: TTM revenue $466.8B (+14.24% YoY), Q3 FY2026 revenue $109.4B (+16.36% YoY), TTM EPS $8.71 (+29.94% YoY), and Q3 gross margin 50.06% / operating margin 32.62%. The core thesis rests on broad-based revenue growth, a high-margin Services mix, and a growing installed base. However, evidence quality is mixed: the claim-level reasoning repeatedly flags that the specific figures cited in claims (e.g., $30.7B Services, 75.6% Services GM, 2.5B installed base, $800M tariff cost) are not directly verifiable from the provided evidence set, and several valuation inputs (forward PE, PS, EV/EBITDA, FCF yield) are unavailable. At PE TTM 37.95 on 14.24% revenue growth, the multiple embeds sustained high growth; the key risk is that growth or margins normalize while the multiple stays elevated. I cannot conclude on forward valuation or on the durability of the tariff/supply-constraint headwinds given missing data.

decisive_variables.why: ~$800M tariff-related costs and iPhone/Mac supply constraints are cited as near-term headwinds; their persistence or resolution directly affects near-term margin and revenue timing. Claim status is only partially_supported.

Tariff costs (~$800M cited) and supply constraints are live headwinds. Watch for margin normalization in the next quarter.

states.name: Revenue growth
states.statement: TTM revenue growth is 14.24% YoY, with Q3 FY2026 revenue up 16.36% YoY to $109.417B.

states.name: Services momentum
states.statement: Services revenue reached $30.7B in Q3 FY2026, up 12% YoY, with records in every services category including cloud and payment services.

states.name: Products growth
states.statement: Products revenue was $78.7B in Q3 FY2026, up 18% YoY, driven by double-digit growth in iPhone and Mac.

states.name: Gross margin pressure from tariffs
states.statement: Company gross margin was 50.1% in Q3 FY2026, including a favorable tariff refund benefit of ~2 percentage points; excluding it, gross margin would have been at the midpoint of guidance. Prior quarter included ~$800M in tariff-related costs.

states.name: Supply constraints
states.statement: Management noted supply constraints on iPhone and, to a lesser extent, Mac in the March quarter, and supply constraints in the June quarter despite double-digit growth in every geographic segment.

states.name: Installed base growth
states.statement: Installed base of over 2.5 billion active devices reached another all-time high across all major product categories and geographic segments.

states.name: Valuation
states.statement: PE TTM is 37.95; forward PE, PS, EV/EBITDA, and FCF yield are unavailable.

What are the actual Services revenue, YoY growth, and gross margin figures for Apple's Q3 FY2026 as reported in the official earnings release or 10-Q?
What were Apple's actual revenue and YoY growth rates for the June 2025 and June 2026 quarters, and what was the TTM revenue growth as of June 2026?
Could Apple's potential server initiative with Nvidia affect its Services or AI strategy?
How sustainable is the Services growth rate and what is the margin mix impact over the next 1-3 years?
What is the quantified impact of tariff-related costs on gross margin going forward?
How much of the recent iPhone and Mac growth is supply-constrained versus demand-driven?
What is the geographic revenue mix and growth by region, especially Greater China and emerging markets?
